facts.statement: The name Dryosaurus comes from Greek words meaning 'tree' and 'lizard', reflecting a presumed forest-dwelling lifestyle rather than the shape of its teeth.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Greek δρῦς, drys, "tree, oak", referring to a presumed forest-dwelling life mode.

facts.statement: Dryosaurus shared its environment with giant sauropods including Brontosaurus, Camarasaurus, and Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: The Morrison Formation records an environment and time dominated by gigantic sauropod dinosaurs such as Brontosaurus, Camarasaurus, Barosaurus, Diplodocus, Apatosaurus and Brachiosaurus.

facts.statement: Dryosaurus lived alongside predators such as Allosaurus, Ceratosaurus, and Torvosaurus.
facts.quote: Predators in this paleoenvironment included the theropods Torvosaurus, Ceratosaurus, Marshosaurus, Stokesosaurus, Ornitholestes and Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Known specimens of Dryosaurus have been estimated to reach lengths of up to 3 meters and weights of up to 100 kilograms.
facts.quote: Based on known specimens, Dryosaurus has been estimated to have reached up to 3 m long and to have weighed up to 100 kg.

facts.statement: Dryosaurus had a horny beak and cheek teeth adapted for processing vegetation.
facts.quote: They had a horny beak and cheek teeth.

facts.statement: Dryosaurus had short arms with five fingers on each hand.
facts.quote: Their arms, however, with five fingers on each hand, were short.

facts.statement: Dryosaurus primarily ate low-growing vegetation found in ancient floodplain environments.
facts.quote: Dryosaurus subsisted primarily on low growing vegetation in ancient floodplains.

facts.statement: Dryosaurus was a quick and agile runner that used its stiff tail as a counterbalance while moving.
facts.quote: A quick and agile runner with strong legs, Dryosaurus used its stiff tail as a counterbalance.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Dryosaurus relied on its speed as its primary defense against carnivorous dinosaurs.
facts.quote: It probably relied on its speed as a main defense against carnivorous dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Some scientists suggest Dryosaurus had cheek-like structures to prevent food loss while chewing.
facts.quote: Some scientists suggest that it had cheek-like structures to prevent the loss of food while the animal processed it in the mouth.

facts.statement: The teeth of Dryosaurus featured a strong median ridge on their lateral surface.
facts.quote: The teeth of Dryosaurus were characterized by a strong median ridge on the lateral surface.

facts.statement: Rodney D. Scheetz and his family discovered a Dryosaurus fossil site near Uravan, Colorado, in 1972.
facts.quote: Rodney D. Scheetz and his family discovered a fossil locality around five miles from Uravan, Colorado in the spring of 1972.

facts.statement: Excavations at the Scheetz site yielded around 2500 fragments, almost all belonging to Dryosaurus.
facts.quote: By then around 2500 fragments had been excavated, almost all of which specimens are thought to have belonged to Dryosaurus.

facts.statement: Fossils from the Scheetz site represent at least eight individuals ranging from juveniles to embryos, with embryonic specimens being exceptionally rare.
facts.quote: At least eight individuals are represented, with ages ranging from juvenile to embryonic; finding specimens of embryonic age is exceptionally rare for dinosaur fossils.

facts.statement: James Leroy Kay and Albert C. Lloyd recovered a Dryosaurus skeleton lacking a skull and neck in 1955.
facts.quote: In 1955 recovered CM 21786, a skeleton lacking skull and neck.

facts.statement: Carpenter and Galton described the Dryosaurus from Dinosaur National Monument as a new species, Dryosaurus elderae, in 2018.
facts.quote: Carpenter and Galton (2018), who described the Dinosaur National Monument Dryosaurus as a new species, D. elderae.

facts.statement: A hatchling found in Utah showed that young Dryosaurus had proportionally large eyes and short muzzles, which changed as they grew.
facts.quote: A Dryosaurus hatchling found at Dinosaur National Monument in Utah confirmed that Dryosaurus followed similar patterns of craniofacial development to other vertebrates; the eyes were proportionally large while young and the muzzle proportionally short.

facts.statement: It is debated or unknown what the true adult size of Dryosaurus was because no adult specimens have been found.
facts.quote: However, as no known adult specimens of the genus have been found, the adult size remains unknown.

facts.statement: Samuel Wendell Williston discovered remains of small euornithopods in Wyoming in 1876.
facts.quote: In 1876, Samuel Wendell Williston in Albany County, Wyoming discovered the remains of small euornithopods.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Dryosaurus was found in the Upper Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation from the Tithonian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, YPM 1876, was found in a layer of the Upper Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation, dating from the Tithonian.

facts.statement: Several fossils from Wyoming have been assigned to the species Dryosaurus altus.
facts.quote: Several other fossils from Wyoming have been referred to Dryosaurus altus.

facts.statement: Dryosaurus fossils have been found at sites including Bone Cabin Quarry, the Red Fork of the Powder River, and Lily Park.
facts.quote: Other sites that have produced Dryosaurus material include Bone Cabin Quarry, the Red Fork of the Powder River in Wyoming and Lily Park in Colorado.

facts.statement: Dryosaurus is a genus of two known species of ornithopod dinosaurs belonging to the Dryosauridae family.
facts.quote: Dryosaurus (gr. "reptil roble") es un género con dos especies conocidas de dinosaurios ornitópodos driosáuridos

facts.statement: Dryosaurus fossils have been found in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Dryosaurus altus was originally named by Marsh in 1978 and remained the only valid species until Carpenter and Galton described Dryosaurus elderae in 2018.
facts.quote: Originalmente llamada Laosaurus altus por Marsh en 1978, Dryosaurus altus fue la única especie válida del género hasta 2018 donde Carpenter y Galton describieran Dryosaurus elderae

facts.statement: Dryosaurus had a light and slender body form with a long neck, hind legs, and tail.
facts.quote: La forma del animal era bastante ligera y esbelta, provista de cuello, patas traseras y cola de gran longitud

facts.statement: Dryosaurus had relatively short forelimbs with a primitive five-fingered hand structure.
facts.quote: Las extremidades superiores, por el contrario, eran bastante cortas y provistas de la dotación primitiva de cinco dedos

facts.statement: Dryosaurus measured between 2.5 and 4.5 meters in total length and stood about 1.5 meters tall at the shoulders.
facts.quote: La longitud total oscilaba entre los 2,5 y 4,5 metros y la altura en los hombros se situaba en torno a 1,5 metros

facts.statement: The total weight of Dryosaurus could reach 80 to 90 kilograms.
facts.quote: El peso total podía llegar a los 80 o 90 kilogramos

facts.statement: The size of adult Dryosaurus is unknown because no known adult specimens of the genus have been found.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el tamaño del adulto es desconocido, ya que no se han encontrado especímenes adultos conocidos del género

facts.statement: Dryosaurus had large eye sockets indicating good vision and a horny beak similar to that of a turtle.
facts.quote: En la cabeza destacan unas grandes cuencas oculares, indicativos de una buena visión y un pico córneo similar al de una tortuga

facts.statement: Dryosaurus teeth were located exclusively at the level of the cheeks and were absent from the premaxilla, a trait also seen in Tenontosaurus.
facts.quote: Los dientes, típicos de otros dinosaurios herbívoros, se situaban exclusivamente a la altura de las mejillas y estaban ausentes del premaxilar

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Dryosaurus cheeks may have been used to store food.
facts.quote: Es posible que las mejillas se utilizasen para guardar alimento

facts.statement: Museum curator John Foster noted that Dryosaurus teeth were characterized by a strong median crest on the lateral surface.
facts.quote: Según el conservador del museo John Foster, los dientes de Dryosaurus se caracterizaron por "una fuerte cresta mediana en la superficie lateral"

facts.statement: Skeletal characteristics indicate Dryosaurus was quite fast, relying on speed as its primary defense against carnivorous theropods.
facts.quote: Las características del esqueleto indican que estos animales eran bastante rápidos y que la velocidad constituía su única arma frente a la acción de los terópodos carnívoros

facts.statement: The always erect tail of Dryosaurus helped maintain balance while running.
facts.quote: La cola, siempre erecta, contribuía a mantener el equilibrio durante la carrera

facts.statement: Fossil sites indicate that Dryosaurus was typically a forest-dwelling animal.
facts.quote: Los yacimientos fósiles indican que Dryosaurus fue un animal típicamente forestal

facts.statement: Dryosaurus subsisted mainly on low vegetation in ancient floodplains.
facts.quote: Dryosaurus subsistió principalmente de vegetación baja en antiguas llanuras de inundación

facts.statement: A Dryosaurus juvenile found in Utah's Dinosaur National Monument confirmed that the species followed craniofacial development patterns similar to other vertebrates.
facts.quote: Una cría de Dryosaurus encontrada en el Monumento Nacional de los Dinosaurios en Utah confirmó que Dryosaurus siguió patrones similares de desarrollo craneofacial a otros vertebrados

facts.statement: Samuel Wendell Williston discovered remains of small euornithopods in Albany County, Wyoming, in 1876.
facts.quote: En 1876, Samuel Wendell Williston en el condado de Albany, Wyoming descubrió los restos de pequeños euornitópodos

facts.statement: Professor Othniel Charles Marsh named the remains a new species of Laosaurus, Laosaurus altus, in 1878.
facts.quote: En 1878, el profesor Othniel Charles Marsh los denominó como una nueva especie de Laosaurus, Laosaurus altus

facts.statement: The specific name 'altus' means 'high' in Latin and refers to the fact that it was larger than Laosaurus celer.
facts.quote: El nombre específico altus , que significa "alto" en latín, se refiere a que es más grande que Laosaurus celer

facts.statement: In 1894, Marsh elevated the taxon to a separate genus named Dryosaurus.
facts.quote: En 1894, Marsh hizo del taxón un género separado, Dryosaurus

facts.statement: The name Dryosaurus comes from Greek words meaning 'oak' and 'lizard', referring to a supposed forest lifestyle.
facts.quote: El nombre proviene del griego δρυο/dryo que significa "roble" y σαυρος/sauros "lagarto", refiriéndose a un supuesto modo de vida en el bosque

facts.statement: It was often supposed that the name referred to an oak leaf shape on its cheeks, but such a feature is absent.
facts.quote: Más tarde, a menudo se suponía que se le había dado el nombre de una forma de hoja de roble de sus mejillas, que, sin embargo, está ausente

facts.statement: The holotype YPM 1876 was found in a layer of the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation, dating to the Tithonian.
facts.quote: El holotipo, YPM 1876, se encontró en una capa del Miembro de la Cuenca Brushy Superior de la Formación Morrison, que data del titoniano

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton including a fairly complete skull and lower jaws.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial que incluye un cráneo bastante completo y mandíbulas inferiores

facts.statement: From 1922 onwards, Earl Douglass discovered Dryosaurus remains in Dinosaur National Monument, Utah.
facts.quote: Desde 1922 en adelante en Utah, Earl Douglass descubrió restos de Dryosaurus en el Monumento nacional Dinosaurio

facts.statement: In 1955, James Leroy Kay and Albert C. Lloyd recovered skeleton CM 21786 in Lily Park, Moffat County, Colorado, which lacked a skull and neck.
facts.quote: Otros fósiles fueron encontrados en Colorado . En Lily Park , condado de Moffat , James Leroy Kay y Albert C. Lloyd en 1955 recuperaron el CM 21786 un esqueleto que carecía de calavera y cuello

facts.statement: In 1973, Peter Malcolm Galton and James Alvin Jensen described specimen BYU ESM-171R found by Rodney Dwayne Scheetz at 'Scheetz' Quarry 1 in Uravan, Montrose County.
facts.quote: Desde 'Scheetz' Quarry 1, en Uravan , condado de Montrose , en 1973 Peter Malcolm Galton y James Alvin Jensen describieron el espécimen BYU ESM-171R encontrado por Rodney Dwayne Scheetzy

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul suggested in his 2010 field guide (second edition published in 2016) that the Utah material represented a separate species.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul en su guía de campo de 2010 para dinosaurios, segunda edición publicada en 2016, sugirió que el material de Utah representaba una especie separada

facts.statement: This suggestion was confirmed by Carpenter and Galton in 2018, who described the Dinosaur National Monument Dryosaurus as a new species, D. elderae.
facts.quote: que fue confirmado por Carpenter y Galton en 2018, quienes describieron el Dryosaurus del monumento nacional de dinosaurio como una nueva especie, D. elderae

facts.statement: The first misnamed species was created accidentally in 1903 when Giuseppe de Stefano renamed Crocodilus phosphaticus Thomas 1893 as Dryosaurus phosphaticus.
facts.quote: La primera de estos fue creada accidentalmente cuando en 1903 Giuseppe de Stefano renombró a Crocodilus phosphaticus Thomas 1893 en Dryosaurus phosphaticus

facts.statement: This error was corrected by Éric Buffetaut in 1981.
facts.quote: Esto fue solo enmendado por Éric Buffetaut en 1981

facts.statement: The species Dryosaurus lettowvorbecki was identified in 1919 by Virchow and named after German military figure Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck.
facts.quote: La especie Dryosaurus lettowvorbecki fue identificada en 1919 por Virchow y llamada así por el afamado militar alemán Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck

facts.statement: Fossils of Dryosaurus lettowvorbecki were found in sites in present-day Tanzania, including Tendaguru.
facts.quote: Fueron encontrados en yacimientos de la actual Tanzania, entre los que se incluye Tendaguru

facts.statement: Dryosaurus lettowvorbecki has now been reassigned to the genus Dysalotosaurus as Dysalotosaurus lettowvorbecki.
facts.quote: Ahora se ha reasignado a Dysalotosaurus como Dysalotosaurus lettowvorbecki

facts.statement: The species Dryosaurus canaliculatus, identified in 1976 from early Cretaceous sites in Europe, was later reassigned to the genus Valdosaurus as Valdosaurus canaliculatus.
facts.quote: La especie Dryosaurus canaliculatus , identificada en 1976 en yacimientos del Cretácico temprano de Europa, fue asignada más tarde al género Valdosaurus como Valdosaurus canaliculatus

facts.statement: Dryosaurus shares size, shape, and bone characteristics with Hypsilophodontidae ornithopods but cannot be included in that family due to special genus characteristics.
facts.quote: Dryosaurus poseen un tamaño, forma y características óseas similares a las de los ornitópodos de la familia Hypsilophodontidae, aunque no puede ser incluido dentro de ésta debido a otros caracteres especiales del género

facts.statement: Therefore, Dryosaurus has been assigned to its own family, Dryosauridae.
facts.quote: Por ello, este dinosaurio ha sido asignado a una familia propia, Dryosauridae

facts.statement: Several of these characteristics appear in Cretaceous iguanodontians, of which Dryosaurus is likely a primitive ancestor or a form close to their immediate ancestors.
facts.quote: Varias de estas características aparecen en los iguanodóntidos del Cretácico, de los que Dryosaurus es probablemente un primitivo ancestro o una forma próxima a sus inmediatos antepasados

facts.statement: A cladogram of Dryosaurus follows the analysis by Paul M. Barrett, Richard J. Butler, Richard J. Twitchett, and Stephen Hutt in 2011.
facts.quote: El siguiente cladograma sigue el análisis de Paul M. Barrett, Richard J. Butler, Richard J. Twitchett y Stephen Hutt (2011)

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Dryosaurus, cataloged as YPM 1876, was discovered in Reed YPM Quarry 5 within the Upper Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo de Dryosaurus YPM 1876 fue descubierto en la cantera 5 de Reed YPM, en el Miembro Cuenca Brushy Superior, de la formación Morrison.

facts.statement: A spectacular excavation site near Uravan, Colorado, contained hundreds of D. altus fossils representing multiple stages of the animal's life cycle.
facts.quote: Un sitio de excavación espectacular cerca de Uravan, Colorado, contenía cientos de fósiles de D. altus que representaban múltiples etapas del ciclo de vida del animal.

facts.statement: The Morrison Formation, where Dryosaurus fossils are found, dates from 156.3 to 146.8 million years ago, corresponding to the late Oxfordian, Kimmeridgian, and early Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Esta formación es una secuencia de sedimentos superficiales marinos y aluviales que, de acuerdo con la datación radiométrica , oscila entre 156,3 millones de años en su base, a 146,8 millones de años en la parte superior, lo que lo sitúa en las etapas finales del Oxfordiense, Kimmeridgiense y Titoniense temprano del período Jurásico superior.

facts.statement: The Morrison Formation is interpreted as a semi-arid environment with distinct wet and dry seasons.
facts.quote: La formación Morrison se interpreta como un entorno semiárido con distintas estaciones húmedas y secas.

facts.statement: The Morrison Basin where Dryosaurus lived extended from New Mexico to Alberta and Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: La cuenca de Morrison donde vivían los dinosaurios, se extendía desde Nuevo México hasta Alberta y Saskatchewan

facts.statement: Dryosaurus lived alongside ornithischian herbivores such as Camptosaurus, Stegosaurus, and Othnielosaurus.
facts.quote: Los dinosaurios que vivieron junto a Dryosaurus incluyen los herbívoros ornitisquios Camptosaurus, Stegosaurus y Othnielosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus Dryosaurus was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1894.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Dryosaurus (genus), Marsh 1894

facts.statement: Dryosaurus belongs to the family Dryosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Dryosauridae

facts.statement: Dryosaurus is classified within the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Dryosaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, approximately 154.8 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 1877, the Morrison Formation became the center of the Bone Wars, a rivalry between paleontologists Othniel Charles Marsh and Edward Drinker Cope.
facts.quote: En 1877, esta formación se convirtió en el centro de las Guerra de los Huesos, una rivalidad entre los paleontólogos Othniel Charles Marsh y Edward Drinker Cope.

facts.statement: Dryosaurus fossils have also been found at the Bone Cabin Quarry, the Red Fork of the Powder River in Wyoming, and Lily Park in Colorado.
facts.quote: Otros sitios que han producido material de Dryosaurus incluyen la cantera Bone Cabin, Red Fork del Powder River en Wyoming y Lily Park en Colorado.

facts.statement: Recent research by Krumenacker et al. (2026) describes three iguanodontian specimens from the Morrison Formation that have a morphology distinct from Dryosaurus and Camptosaurus.
facts.quote: Three iguanodontian specimens with a morphology distinct from those of members of the genera Dryosaurus and Camptosaurus are described from the strata of the Morrison Formation from the Simon Quarry (Wyoming, United States) by Krumenacker et al. (2026).
